about.title: Developer and teacher
about.text: I’m a developer and a teacher. For more than 5 years I’ve been building web and mobile apps — from company websites to CRMs and internal tools. For the last 4 years I’ve worked at Stanford private school, where I’m now Head of IT: I set the standards for our lessons and build the school’s digital tools myself. I love turning messy processes run on spreadsheets and paper into clear systems that save people time.

projects.subtitle: A weekly assessment platform for a private school: ~400 students, 5 roles and a Telegram bot for parents.
projects.text: I moved the system from Google Sheets and Apps Script to Laravel + React with no data loss and scores that match to the point. Students take tests on school computers, teachers manage the question bank, and parents get their child’s weekly card right in Telegram.

projects.student.p1: The timer runs on the server — reloading the page doesn’t reset it

projects.teacher.p2: Bulk upload of questions from a file

projects.parent.p2: Percentages only — no grades and no red
projects.telegram.p1: A weekly picture card for every student
projects.telegram.p2: The card is rendered in the browser (SVG → JPEG) and sent without re-uploading
projects.arch.title: How it works
projects.arch.alt: Diagram: students, teachers, admins and parents use React + Inertia talking to a Laravel API; the API stores data in MySQL/PostgreSQL and Redis and connects to the Telegram bot, Excel import/export and a Google Sheets report.
projects.decisions.title: Interesting decisions
projects.decision1.title: Exact scoring
projects.decision1.text: Final scores combine the test and written work with per-subject weights; rounding matches the old system to the point.
projects.decision2.title: Reliable submission
projects.decision2.text: Server-side time and writes in a locked transaction: a double click never creates a second attempt.
projects.decision3.title: Duplicate-free import
projects.decision3.text: Uploading the same Excel file again duplicates nothing — rows are matched by hash.
projects.decision4.title: Security
projects.decision4.text: Codes are stored as HMAC hashes, brute force is throttled and permissions are checked on every action.
